newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark must hold 1.7225 or slide further.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark must hold 1.7225 or slide further.

text.p: For a second session the dollar tested key support at 1.7225 marks, risking a tumble down to 1.7150 marks and perhaps even below 1.71, technical analysts said on Thursday.
But some chartists were optimistic the 1.7225 prop would hold, setting up a mild dollar rally.

"From 1.7225 to 1.72 is good support and I suspect it hangs in there. As long as we hold above that level for the next day or so, the dollar will rally back up," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America
Meanwhile, the dollar staged a mini-comeback against the yen, hurdling 114 and approaching resistance at 114.40.

"Closing above 113.80 would be constructive; closing above 114.40 would be very positive and perhaps mean a test of the trendline at 114.80/90," said John Tirone, a technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.
Dollar/yen has been in a long-term bearish phase, falling nearly 12 percent from its May 1 high of 127.47, and a break above the 114.40 yen ceiling would not necessarily signal a reversal.

At 1400 EDT, the dollar rose to 114.11/21 yen from 113.32/42 at the open, but below its session high of 114.30. After a brief foray higher, the dollar fell to 1.7235/40 marks from 1.7300/10 at the open.
Tirone was quick to note that big picture, dollar/mark remains mired in a 1.70 to 1.7440 trading range. A break of the 1.7423 39-month high made on June 6 is needed to mark a fresh rally.
"Nothing is going to happen until we get aboove 1.7440 on the upside and on the downside, we're really testing a daily trendline at 1.7220," Tirone said.
Johnson said 1.73 marks has been acting like a pivot point recently but layers of resistance still lie at 1.7370 and 1.74 marks.
